answer.answer:
Found on gov.uk under the 'Child Benefit' guide (https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit):

HOW IT WORKS: You get Child Benefit if you're responsible for bringing up a child who is under 16, or under 20 if they stay in approved education or training. Only one person can claim per child, but there's no limit on how many children you can claim for. Claiming gives you: (1) an allowance paid every 4 weeks, (2) National Insurance credits counting towards your State Pension (automatic if your child is under 12), and (3) a National Insurance number automatically issued to your child near their 16th birthday. Even if you opt out of payments (e.g. due to High Income Child Benefit Charge), you should still claim to get these other benefits. You must report any change of circumstances to the Child Benefit Office.

ELIGIBILITY (Who can get Child Benefit) - https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility: You normally qualify if you're responsible for a child under 16 and live in the UK. You're 'responsible' if you live with the child or pay at least as much as Child Benefit towards their upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money). Special rules apply if the child goes into hospital/care, lives with someone else, is 16/17 and leaves education (20-week extension possible if registering with a careers service or armed forces), is fostered (as long as the council isn't paying for accommodation/maintenance), is being adopted (can claim once child moves in, before adoption finalized), or is an informally cared-for friend/relative's child. Only one person can claim per child - HMRC decides if there's a dispute. Additional rules apply for people living abroad, those with settled/pre-settled EU status, workers, jobseekers (91-day allowance), students, and family members of EEA/Swiss nationals. Benefit stops if the child starts full-time paid work (24+ hrs/week), an apprenticeship, or claims certain benefits themselves.

HOW TO CLAIM (Make a claim) - https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim: You can claim 48 hours after registering the birth, or once a child comes to live with you. Claims can be backdated up to 3 months. Only one person per household should claim (whoever claims gets the NI credits); couples should decide who claims, especially regarding the higher rate for the eldest child. Claims can be made online via the 'Make a claim online' service (requires sign-in via Government Gateway - not accessed per task instructions), or by post/phone as alternatives. Before starting you need: child's birth/adoption certificate (if available), bank/building society details, your National Insurance number, and your partner's NI number if applicable. You can still claim without the birth certificate (claim will be backdated once document is later provided). If the child's birth was registered outside the UK, you need the original birth/adoption certificate plus the child's passport or travel document used to enter the UK.

Note: The actual online claim form requires signing in and entering personal data, so per the task instructions I stopped at the 'Make a claim' page without clicking 'Start now' or proceeding further.
